name: M-Audio Code 61
note: Code 61 (Code 49/25 run the same firmware): an STM32F103RB-class part (or a GD32F103RB clone), 128 KB flash in 1 KB pages, 20 KB RAM, 8 MHz HSE. The vendor layout: M-Audio's bootloader (or gemifi's, bootloader/stm32f1) in the first 9 KB, the app up to the vendor's image-checksum page 0x0801B000, the vendor settings 'EEPROM' 0x0801B400-0x0801FBFF, and the update-request flag page 0x0801FC00. The board header (m-audio-code61.h) has the power latch code; research/devices/m-audio-code61/analysis/ has the pins.

flash.note: app_end: the page at 0x0801B000 belongs to the vendor update (whole-image checksum at 0x0801B3FE), so the link stops below it; image_max is the vendor's app area, up to the checksum. Config: the three pages 0x0801EC00-0x0801F7FF that the stock app never touches, inside the vendor 'EEPROM' window (its calibration and preset pages stay intact); 0x0801F800 is the vendor's preset-names page: never used. Earlier firmware used the first two pages as a swap pair; that layout is read as it is. The pages may hold old data on a real unit: config_store only trusts magic + CRC records and erases a page before writing into it again. Capacity (the builder's storage budget): every slot's newest record together (L) and the largest one (M) give L + M <= 2 x 1024 B, so about 5 worst-case presets + the globals. Under gemifi's own bootloader the vendor pages are free too, but stock-bootloader units can't use them.

soft_power.note: PC13 = power button, input pull-up, low while pressed; PC15 = power latch, push-pull, high = stay on. Verified over SWD 2026-11-03. board_gpio_init() latches it at reset; held 2 s = off (app and bootloader).

recovery.what: Up + Down held at reset (matrix row 16)
recovery.note: No panel button is on a plain GPIO: PB3-PB7 low select decoder row 16 (address 0, both group selects low), the columns PB8-PB15 are pulled up, and PB8 + PB9 both low = Up and Down held (confirmed on hardware 2026-11-03). PB3/PB4 are JTAG pins at reset.
